avs.prompt: As a Pre-lesson Vocabulary Warm-up, one of the strategies is to let the learner go through Anchor Vocabulary Set (AVS) rather than conventional difficult words list. Here's an extremely lean "mental warm-up" before reading, anchors essentially give the learner the visual skeleton of the entire story before they encounter the prose. Return one single json set in any array with their one line explanation.
avs.anchorVocabularySet:
[
  {"anchor": "rich landlord", "explanation": "A wealthy man who owns a lot of land."},
  {"anchor": "large tracts of land", "explanation": "Very large areas of land owned by someone."},
  {"anchor": "look after the land", "explanation": "Take care of the land and manage it."},
  {"anchor": "magic potion", "explanation": "A special magical liquid believed to have extraordinary powers."},
  {"anchor": "turn objects into gold", "explanation": "Change an ordinary object into valuable gold."},
  {"anchor": "spend all his money", "explanation": "Use up a large amount of money while searching for something."},
  {"anchor": "worried wife", "explanation": "A wife who fears that her family may run out of money."},
  {"anchor": "famous sage", "explanation": "A wise and respected person believed to possess special knowledge."},
  {"anchor": "Himalayas", "explanation": "The great mountain region where the sage says he learned about the potion."},
  {"anchor": "banana plant", "explanation": "A plant that Rama Natha must grow as part of the process."},
  {"anchor": "water regularly", "explanation": "Give the banana plants water again and again as they grow."},
  {"anchor": "morning dew", "explanation": "Tiny drops of water that appear on leaves in the early morning."},
  {"anchor": "collect dew from leaves", "explanation": "Gather the tiny drops of dew from the banana leaves."},
  {"anchor": "five litres", "explanation": "A very large quantity of dew that Rama Natha must collect."},
  {"anchor": "magic words â gold", "explanation": "The sage will use magical words to turn the collected dew into a potion that can make gold."}
]

avsVisual.prompt: Create a single 9:16 infographic-style 'story skeleton' depicting the flow of all AVS anchors below, in order. Lay out a bold title banner at the top naming the story's arc, with a subtitle noting the anchor count (e.g. 'N Anchor Vocabulary Points (AVS)'). Below it, render each anchor as its own rounded, color-bordered card containing: a numbered circle badge, the anchor phrase as a colored title, a small relevant illustration, and its one-line explanation beneath. Arrange the cards in numbered reading order, connected by curved arrows showing the story's flow from card to card, wrapping row by row. The final card should visually culminate the story's resolution. Close with a short one-line takeaway/moral banner at the bottom. Use a warm, colorful, semi-illustrative (not photorealistic) style appropriate for the target class level, with no text beyond the card titles/explanations and the banners described.

avsAssessment.prompt: As a cognitive assessment, create a suitable 9:16 visual image of random 5 from the AVS, by depicting the actual visual side by side a contrasting visual to test the vocabulary of the learner. Should be in 3x5 grid format and make the ordering of the right and wrong visual random such that the learner does not assume that the first one is always right. Also return a json of answer.  DO NOT: add any text overlay on image that will help the learner to identify the right visual. Also DO NOT use any real life character visual. Also DO NOT use any distant relation visual for the wrong one but a close resembling one to confuse the learner.  DO NOT OMIT the AVS item show (ANCHOR ONLY, NO EXPLANATION, NO IMAGE) in the first cell of each row. DO NOT SHOW ANY HUMAN AS ANIMAL CHARACTER. Ensure that the correct option image is NOT debatable.

sensoryWarmup.prompt: As a Pre-lesson Sensory Warm-up, reuse the Vocabulary Warm-up's own visual (preLessonWarmup.vocabularyWarmup.avsVisual.image) rather than generating a separate scene image -- the learner has just studied that image card-by-card, so this activity asks them to step back and look at it as a whole. Within a 2-minute window, the learner types or dictates, in their own words, what story they think this flow of anchors is telling, before the actual story is introduced.
sensoryWarmup.responsePrompt: Look at the Vocabulary Warm-Up image again, as a whole. Based on what you see, type or say what you think this story might be about.

experientialWarmup.prompt: For experiential warmup, the goal is to allow the learner relate personal experience to the morale of the story. The story tagline can stay as is. Frame 3 questions for experiential warmup, all provide cues (micro questions) to the learner regarding the flow of the reflection. Return it in a json format.

questions.question: Think of a time when you hoped for an easy shortcut but later realized that steady effort was the better way. What happened?
cues: What were you trying to achieve?
What shortcut did you hope to find?
What work did you finally do?
What did the experience teach you?

questions.question: Recall a time when your regular hard work led to a result you were proud of. How did your effort make a difference?
cues: What result did your effort produce?

questions.question: Think of a time when someone guided you toward a better way of doing something. How did their guidance help you?
cues: What advice or task did they give you?
How did you respond at first?
What did you learn after following their guidance?

holisticAssessment.prompt: As a Post-lesson holistic assessment, re-test the learner's mastery of the full Anchor Vocabulary Set now that the story has been read. Reuse the same 9:16, 3x5 side-by-side visual grid mechanic as the pre-lesson AVS assessment, covering all 15 anchors across 3 batches, but raise the rigor: use closer-resembling distractor visuals than the pre-lesson version, and vary the correct-option pattern across rows and batches so a learner cannot pattern-match position instead of reading the anchor. Same constraints as before: no text overlay revealing the answer, no real-life character visuals, no human-as-animal depictions, correct option must not be debatable, and show the AVS anchor (text only, no explanation) in the first cell of each row.

transferablePatterns.prompt: You are a learning architect. Critically review the story. Return in a structured json the most important transferrable patterns

storyAnchorQuestions.prompt: Create a list of questions using the suitable format for the item being listed (mcq / true false / fill in the blanks / reorder / assertion / short answer / HOTS (recall / infer / predict) / etc.) from the story anchor point from each sentence in the prose. Return in a structured json format.
